html:
The Lipan are an eastern Apache people of the southern Plains, who lived in what is now Texas and northern Mexico.

In the 1600s they hunted bison and farmed on the southern Plains. In the 1700s the Comanche and their allies pushed them south into central and south Texas and across the Rio Grande into Coahuila. The Lipan raided and traded with Spanish Texas, and at times sought its help. In 1757 Spain built the San Sabá mission for them; the next year Comanche and allied warriors destroyed it.

Wars with Mexico, Texas and the United States in the 1800s nearly wiped them out. Survivors joined the Mescalero in New Mexico. Today descendants also live in Texas, where they call themselves Ndé.
sum: The Lipan are an eastern Apache people of the southern Plains, who lived in what is now Texas and northern Mexico.
